doc.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1959-05-25

title: Carrie Boote remembers the 1878 yellow fever epidemic
summary: Carrie recalls the silent town, no bells, and playmates dying of yellow fever.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When you're ready, just go ahead. You want to tell about that clipping? Oh, this? Yellow fever?

Well, I said that the... That was in May when... Well, all that I can say, I remember that time and date, you know, in 1878, when the yellow people were so bad that the trains wasn't... The bells wasn't ringing on the steam cars and the town was all quiet. No bells or whatsoever. The people were dying three and four into the homes. And I visited family one day, went back the next day to play with my little comrades and they were all dead. They were white right at the corner. Good children, we called it.
